theory.intro: Angles use the **sexagesimal** system, based on sixties: $60$ seconds make a minute and $60$ minutes make a degree. Because a degree splits into $60$ parts rather than $10$, the halfway mark for rounding is $30$.
facts: To change a decimal part of a degree into minutes, multiply it by $60$: $0.35^{\circ}=0.35\times 60=21'$.
Rounding to the nearest degree makes the minutes the **critical unit**; rounding to the nearest minute makes the seconds the critical unit.
**$30$ is the halfway mark**: round down if the critical unit is less than $30$, and up if it is $30$ or more.
Rounding up from $59'$ gives $60'$, which is a whole degree: $46^{\circ}\,59'\,38''\approx 47^{\circ}\,0'$.
steps: Circle the critical unit right after the cut
Round up if the critical unit is $30$ or more, down if it is less

workedExamples.question_text:
Round each angle to the nearest degree.
(a) $26^{\circ}\,19'$
(b) $48^{\circ}\,42'\,9''$
(c) $63^{\circ}\,30'$
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Cut after the degrees: $26^{\circ}\,|\,19'$. The critical unit is $19'$. Since $19<30$, round down: $26^{\circ}\,19'\approx26^{\circ}$.

(b) Cut after the degrees: $48^{\circ}\,|\,42'\,9''$. The critical unit is $42'$. Since $42\geq30$, round up: $48^{\circ}\,42'\,9''\approx49^{\circ}$.

(c) Cut after the degrees: $63^{\circ}\,|\,30'$. Exactly $30'$ is halfway, so round up: $63^{\circ}\,30'\approx64^{\circ}$.

workedExamples.question_text:
Round each angle to the nearest minute.
(a) $32^{\circ}\,14'\,21''$
(b) $57^{\circ}\,28'\,46''$
(c) $81^{\circ}\,7'\,30''$
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Cut after the minutes: $32^{\circ}\,14'\,|\,21''$. The critical unit is $21''$. Since $21<30$, round down: $32^{\circ}\,14'\,21''\approx32^{\circ}\,14'$.

(b) Cut after the minutes: $57^{\circ}\,28'\,|\,46''$. Since $46\geq30$, round up: $57^{\circ}\,28'\,46''\approx57^{\circ}\,29'$.

(c) Cut after the minutes: $81^{\circ}\,7'\,|\,30''$. Exactly $30''$ is halfway, so round up: $81^{\circ}\,7'\,30''\approx81^{\circ}\,8'$.

Keep the $46$ whole degrees. Multiply the decimal part by $60$ to find the minutes.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}0.65\times60\\&=39\end{aligned}$
The decimal part represents $39'$.
$46.65^{\circ}=46^{\circ}\,39'$

workedExamples.question_text:
Write each angle to the nearest minute.
(a) $38.372^{\circ}$
(b) $69.4585^{\circ}$
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Convert the decimal part to minutes.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}0.372\times60\\&=22.32\end{aligned}$
Keep $22'$ and convert the remaining $0.32'$ to seconds.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}0.32\times60\\&=19.2\end{aligned}$
Cut after the minutes: $38^{\circ}\,22'\,|\,19.2''$. Since $19.2<30$, round down: $38.372^{\circ}\approx38^{\circ}\,22'$.

(b) Convert the decimal part to minutes.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}0.4585\times60\\&=27.51\end{aligned}$
Keep $27'$ and convert the remaining $0.51'$ to seconds.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}0.51\times60\\&=30.6\end{aligned}$
Cut after the minutes: $69^{\circ}\,27'\,|\,30.6''$. Since $30.6\geq30$, round up: $69.4585^{\circ}\approx69^{\circ}\,28'$.

workedExamples.question_text:
Round each angle to the nearest minute.
(a) $34^{\circ}\,59'\,36''$
(b) $76.996^{\circ}$
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Cut after the minutes: $34^{\circ}\,59'\,|\,36''$. Since $36\geq30$, round up. This gives $60'$, which is one whole degree.
$\begin{aligned}34^{\circ}\,59'\,36''&\approx34^{\circ}\,60'\\&=35^{\circ}\,0'\end{aligned}$

(b) Convert the decimal part to minutes.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}0.996\times60\\&=59.76\end{aligned}$
Convert the remaining $0.76'$ to seconds.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}0.76\times60\\&=45.6\end{aligned}$
Cut after the minutes: $76^{\circ}\,59'\,|\,45.6''$. Since $45.6\geq30$, round up and exchange $60'$ for one degree.
$\begin{aligned}76.996^{\circ}&\approx76^{\circ}\,60'\\&=77^{\circ}\,0'\end{aligned}$
